record.title: IQM reports a vision-language workflow calibrating all 20 qubits on one processor
record.summary: IQM's Oct. 21 case study reports connecting NVIDIA Ising Calibration vision-language models to IQM calibration software and running the workflow on one 20-qubit processor. IQM says the system widened measurement ranges for qubits whose settings fell outside chart ranges, reran those measurements and finished with all 20 qubits calibrated. The report provides no calibration-quality metric, elapsed time, matched expert baseline or independent reproduction, so it supports an attributed account of one run rather than a performance or generalization result.

evidence_gaps.description: No run-level calibration quality, wall-clock, intervention, failure or matched expert-comparison data were found in the case study.
The reported physical-chip workflow has not been independently reproduced in this review.

The QCalEval dataset card describes hybrid simulated and partner-hardware data, while NVIDIA Ising Calibration 1.5 model cards label QCalEval evaluation data synthetic with simulation-derived ground truth. The official rows API returned all 243 test records; their exposed schema has no row-level hardware/synthetic provenance field, leaving the composition unresolved.

brief.importance_rationale: If the reported workflow is repeatable, a vision-language agent that reads calibration plots, selects follow-up experiments, adjusts ranges and operates real quantum hardware could reduce a scarce expert bottleneck and broaden access to quantum-computing operations. The evidence is a single partner-reported 20-qubit case with no published calibration metrics, timing, matched human comparison or independent reproduction.
limitations: This is a single first-party partner case study from IQM, which participated in the work; no independent confirmation of the physical run was identified.
The report gives no calibration fidelity or quality metric, wall-clock time, human-intervention count, failure rate or matched expert baseline.
The exact Ising model version and public run-level logs or complete workflow artifacts are not identified.
IQM says larger chips and problems beyond engineer-recognizable cases remain future/open work; this report does not establish generalization.

QCalEval is a separate chart-understanding benchmark and is not an independent replication of the reported chip run. Its public dataset card describes a hybrid collection of simulations and partner-supplied hardware measurements, while NVIDIA Ising Calibration 1.5 model cards describe QCalEval evaluation data as synthetic with simulation-derived ground truth. The public viewer shows 243 test rows with experiment identifiers and families but no visible row-level provenance field; sample-level composition and any connection to the IQM run remain unresolved.

technical.claimed_result: IQM reports that the workflow calibrated all 20 qubits on one IQM processor and logged decisions in plain English. The report does not provide calibration-quality measures, wall-clock time, expert comparison or failure statistics.
technical.compute_or_cost: No wall-clock, compute, labor or cost comparison is reported.
technical.demonstrated_result: The inspected first-party IQM page documents that IQM made this case-study report and describes the workflow and its limits. This inspection does not independently establish the physical run's outcome.
technical.implementation_status: A partner-reported experiment connected the model to proprietary calibration software; public run logs, full workflow artifacts and exact model version were not identified.
technical.mechanism: IQM says NVIDIA Ising Calibration vision-language models were connected to IQM's calibration software. When parameters for some qubits fell outside chart ranges, the workflow reportedly widened those ranges and reran the measurements.
technical.novelty: The report describes a vision-language model selecting measurement-range adjustments in a physical quantum calibration workflow. This is a source-reported use case, not an independently verified performance advance.
technical.regime: One IQM 20-qubit chip and a case-study workflow involving engineer-recognizable calibration plots. The report does not establish operation on larger chips, unseen problem types or other hardware.
technical.reproducibility: The public case study does not provide sufficient run logs, quality criteria or complete workflow artifacts to reproduce the chip experiment. QCalEval is a separate plot benchmark and does not independently reproduce this run.
technical.strongest_baseline: No matched expert calibration baseline or conventional workflow result is reported.
